tiktok-video-downloader.intro: The TikTok Video Downloader saves a public TikTok video to your device in the same quality the app plays it, without the logo overlay that the in-app Save button burns in. Paste a link, and the original MP4 is fetched straight from TikTok's servers — no account, no app, no re-encoding.

sections.p:
When you tap Share and Copy link in TikTok, you get a URL that points at a specific post. This tool reads the public metadata TikTok exposes for that post and locates the address of the original video file — the exact file the app streams when you watch. It then hands you that file as-is.

That distinction matters. The clip you get from the app's own Save button has the username and logo composited into the picture. The file this downloader returns is the clean upload, so it is ready to archive, re-edit, or repost elsewhere without a second platform's branding stamped on it.

TikTok stores uploads as MP4 with the H.264 codec, usually 1080×1920 when filmed vertically on a recent phone. You get the best version that exists for that post. If the creator uploaded in 1080p, you download 1080p; if they filmed in 720p, that is the real ceiling and no tool can invent detail that was never captured.

Long links (tiktok.com/@user/video/…), and the short vm.tiktok.com and vt.tiktok.com links the mobile app generates, all resolve. Links that point at a profile or a hashtag do not, because they do not identify a single video. Re-shortened links from other services are not supported.

Only download content you have the right to save. Personal archiving and offline viewing are common; republishing someone else's work as your own, or using it commercially without permission, can infringe copyright. Give the creator credit when you share.

Use a stable connection, confirm the link points to a single public video, and allow the download if your browser prompts you. On iPhone, Safari is the most reliable browser for saving files. If a download stalls, delete the partial file and retry rather than stacking attempts, which can confuse the browser's download queue.

This downloader skips that step and points at the original asset, so you get the clean upload with its full resolution and audio. The difference is invisible on a quick view but obvious when you edit, print, or repost.

A weak connection can also stall a large file, so retry on a stable network.

Yes. There is no charge, no account, and no premium tier, regardless of video length. You paste a public link and save the original file at no cost. The free model applies to long videos just as it does to short ones, so extended content is not gated behind payment.
Will quality drop for long videos?

No, the original quality is preserved. The tool fetches the creator's uploaded file without recompression, so a long 1080p video stays 1080p. The only practical difference is size: longer, higher-resolution files are larger and take more time and space. Quality itself is unchanged from the source.
What if the download stalls?

A large transfer can stall on a slow or unstable connection. If that happens, delete the partial file and retry on a stronger network. Because long videos are big, a stable connection matters more than for short clips. Once the transfer completes, the file plays at the original quality with no watermark.
